title: Confirming HSC strong lens candidates with DESI Spectroscopy. II. Analysis of 80 galaxy-scale systems with lens redshifts above 0.8
summary: The total mass distribution of galaxies provides a sensitive probe of the fundamental physical processes governing galaxy evolution, including gas inflow/star formation, AGN/SN feedback, galaxy merging, and the nature of dark matter. State-of-the-art cosmological simulations have therefore made extensive predictions for the evolution of the total-mass density slope. Interestingly, their predictions diverge significantly at high redshift, primarily due to differences in how these key physical mechanisms are implemented. However, measurements of the total-mass structure evolution have been largely confined to low and intermediate redshifts, leaving the regime where model predictions differ most significantly (z>0.8) largely unexplored. In the first paper of this series, we reported the discovery of 84 candidate strong-lens systems with lens redshifts above 0.8. In this work, we perform lens modeling of the 80 galaxy-scale systems to assess their lensing nature. Of these, 71 systems (approximately 90%) exhibit clear lensing features that are well reproduced by our lens models and are therefore classified as secure strong lenses. Another eight systems are classified as probable (5) or possible (3) strong lenses, based on the prominence of their lensing features and the quality of the lens modeling. One system lacking reliable lensing features in current imaging data is classified as a non-lens. Our analysis nearly triples the number of known galaxy-scale strong lenses at z_lens > 0.8, making statistical studies of the total mass structure of high-redshift galaxies possible for the first time. This expanded sample provides an unprecedented opportunity to test the predictions of cosmological simulations and discriminate between competing physical prescriptions.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 星系的总质量分布为探测主导星系演化的基本物理过程提供了灵敏的探针，这些过程包括气体流入/恒星形成、AGN/SN反馈、星系并合以及暗物质的性质。因此，最先进的宇宙学模拟对总质量密度斜率的演化做出了大量预测。有趣的是，这些预测在高红移处显著分歧，主要源于这些关键物理机制实现方式的差异。然而，对总质量结构演化的测量大多局限于低红移和中等红移，使得模型预测差异最显著的区间（z>0.8）在很大程度上未被探索。在本系列的第一篇论文中，我们报告了84个透镜红移高于0.8的候选强透镜系统。在这项工作中，我们对其中80个星系尺度系统进行透镜建模，以评估其透镜性质。其中，71个系统（约90%）展现出清晰的透镜特征，且与我们的透镜模型吻合良好，因此被归类为确凿的强透镜。另外八个系统根据其透镜特征的显著性和透镜建模的质量被归类为可能的（5个）或潜在的（3个）强透镜。一个在当前成像数据中缺乏可靠透镜特征的系统被归类为非透镜。我们的分析使已知的z_lens > 0.8星系尺度强透镜数量几乎增加了两倍，首次使得对高红移星系总质量结构的统计研究成为可能。这一扩展样本为检验宇宙学模拟的预测并区分竞争性物理方案提供了前所未有的机会。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 基于现有摘要，该工作使已知z_lens>0.8的星系尺度强透镜数量增加近三倍，首次使高红移星系总质量结构的统计研究成为可能，为检验宇宙学模拟预测、区分竞争性物理方案提供了前所未有的机会。

title: The Carousel Lens III: Joint lens convergence and source kinematic modeling
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables, submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: We introduce a new, independent modeling component to the Carousel Lens series by exploiting the spatially-resolved kinematics contained within the lensed arcs, which so far has remained rather underexplored in strong-lensing analyses. We present an end-to-end forward-modeling framework that reconstructs an integral-field spectroscopic datacube from a parameterization of the lens convergence profile together with the line-of-sight velocity, velocity dispersion, and surface brightness profiles of the unlensed source. The kinematic structure of the source acts as an additional set of ray-traceable markers distributed across every lensed image, inaccessible from imaging data alone. Furthermore, by generating an [OII] emission-line datacube, we isolate a single source redshift and remove lens and line-of-sight light contamination. We apply this framework to deep VLT/MUSE observations of the Carousel Lens, modeling the [OII] emission of the quadruply-imaged star-forming galaxy at $z_{\rm s} = 1.432$ that anchors the system's cosmography constraints. We measure an Einstein radius $θ_{\rm E} = 12.816''^{+0.005}_{-0.007}$ and a logarithmic slope $γ= 1.412^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$, tightening the statistical uncertainties on both by roughly a factor of $2-2.5$ relative to the corresponding flat emission-line map model. We find that the source galaxy exhibits a strong rotation, lies confidently along the star-forming main sequence, and has an inferred central black hole mass of $\log M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot} = 7.89 \pm 0.51$. These results establish datacube-level forward modeling as a practical and independent route to traditional image-based lens models in the current systematics-limited regime, and one that extends naturally to this system's other lensed sources and to other lens systems.

AI.tldr: 该文提出一种端到端的积分视场光谱数据立方前向建模方法，利用透镜弧中的空间分辨运动学作为独立建模成分，应用于Carousel Lens的[OII]发射，将爱因斯坦半径和对数斜率的不确定度较平坦发射线图模型收紧约2–2.5倍。
AI.motivation: 强透镜分析中，透镜弧内蕴含的空间分辨运动学信息长期未被充分利用；传统图像模型缺少源内部可追踪的标记，且存在系统误差限制，需要独立于成像建模的新途径。
AI.method: 构建端到端前向建模框架：以透镜收敛度剖面参数化，结合未透镜源的视向速度、速度弥散和表面亮度剖面，重建积分视场光谱数据立方；通过生成[OII]发射线数据立方隔离单一源红移并去除透镜与视线光污染；应用于VLT/MUSE对Carousel Lens的深度观测，建模z_s=1.432的四重成像恒星形成星系。
AI.result: 测得爱因斯坦半径θ_E=12.816''(+0.005/-0.007)、对数斜率γ=1.412(+0.002/-0.002)，统计不确定度较平坦发射线图模型收紧约2–2.5倍；源星系呈强旋转、位于恒星形成主序上，中心黑洞质量log M_BH/M_⊙=7.89±0.51。
AI.conclusion: 数据立方级前向建模可作为独立于传统图像透镜模型的实用路径，并自然推广至该系统其他透镜源及其他透镜系统。

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们通过利用透镜弧内包含的空间分辨运动学信息，为旋转木马透镜系列引入了一个新的、独立的建模组件，这在强透镜分析中迄今尚未得到充分探索。我们提出了一个端到端的前向建模框架，该框架从透镜收敛轮廓的参数化以及未透镜源沿视线速度、速度弥散和表面亮度轮廓出发，重建积分场光谱数据立方。源的运动学结构作为一组额外的可光线追踪标记，分布在每个透镜图像中，这是仅凭成像数据无法获得的。此外，通过生成[OII]发射线数据立方，我们分离出单一源红移，并去除透镜和视线光污染。我们将此框架应用于旋转木马透镜的深度VLT/MUSE观测，对锚定该系统宇宙学约束的四重成像恒星形成星系在$z_{\rm s} = 1.432$处的[OII]发射进行建模。我们测得爱因斯坦半径$θ_{\rm E} = 12.816''^{+0.005}_{-0.007}$和对数斜率$γ= 1.412^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$，相对于相应的平坦发射线图模型，两者的统计不确定性均收紧约$2-2.5$倍。我们发现源星系表现出强旋转，确信位于恒星形成主序上，并推断其中心黑洞质量为$\log M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot} = 7.89 \pm 0.51$。这些结果确立了数据立方级前向建模作为当前系统误差限制区域中传统基于图像的透镜模型的一种实用且独立的途径，并且该途径自然可扩展到该系统的其他透镜源以及其他透镜系统。
artifacts.conclusion_zh: 数据立方级前向建模可作为独立于传统图像透镜模型的实用路径，并自然推广至该系统其他透镜源及其他透镜系统。

figures.caption_en: Figure 1: VLT/MUSE images of the Carousel Lens. Left: the full whitelight image, generated by aggregating the datacube along its spectral axis. The most-prominent galaxy-cluster members are labeled here, with \(L_{e}\) lying outside the image cutout. This is similar to what is typically observed with imaging data. Right: by focusing on the [O II ] emission at \(z_{s}=1.432\) and leveraging the continuum of the other sources in frame, we can generate an image that isolates the source-of-interest S4. Note that source galaxy 5 lies at the same redshift as S4, hence the extra arc to the southeast and image to the southwest within the cutout; we simply mask out these images in our modeling scheme. We also introduce the same labeling of the S4 lensed images as the Carousel Lens Papers 41 , 31 , and 51 .

title: VENUS: Strong Lens Mass Models and Einstein Radii of 60 Galaxy Clusters
summary: We present the strong lens mass modeling result of 60 galaxy clusters targeted by Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) multi-epoch Treasury program. We obtain refined mass models for the 60 clusters with the glafic software by fitting positions of $\sim 4500$ multiple images, $\sim 1150$ of which are newly identified multiple images with help of multi-band JWST images. Each cluster contains typically $\sim 50$ multiple images, thanks to the selection of target clusters based on their high lensing strengths. We validate our models with the Jackknife method. The median Einstein radius is $\sim 30''$ and the distribution of the Einstein radii extends out to $\sim 60''$ for the source redshift of 9, which confirms that their lensing strengths are indeed among the highest known to date. For the source redshift of 9, we identify MACS J0717.5+3745, MACS J0600.1$-$2008, and PLCK G287.0+32.9 as clusters with the largest Einstein radii as well as the largest areas of the high-magnification ($|μ|>10$) regions. We find that the observed Einstein radii of VENUS clusters are fully compatible with the standard cold dark matter model.

title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). Refining the strong lens sample with Space Warps crowd-sourced science
summary: We demonstrate the efficacy of crowd-sourced refinement of strong gravitational lens candidate samples by citizen scientists. Binary (lens/non-lens) classification by citizen scientists has been conducted previously, and here we extend such categorisation into `definite', `probable', `possible', and `non-lenses'. This grading is a required stage ahead of any strong lens sample publication and is usually carried out by (small) teams of researchers. We compare the responses of the volunteers to those of strong lens researchers and discuss the optimal strategy for lens classification and grading in future strong lens searches. Volunteers are found to be able to correctly identify systems of each grade, and their responses can be calibrated to be comparable to those of researchers. Grade posteriors, defined as the probability that a strong lens system classified by the volunteers is a certain grade, converge most rapidly for non-lens systems. We find that one researcher classification is equivalent to only 1.9 volunteer classifications when grading such systems. There is significant disagreement in the grading of intermediate-grade lens candidates amongst both volunteers and researchers. Moving towards calibrated lens probabilities for future lens searches would help to account for such subjectivity. If the Q1 lens search was rerun with volunteers performing lens grading (and corresponding calibration), a completeness of 79% for Grades A+B (corresponding to definite + probable lenses respectively) could be achieved with 41% purity prior to researcher inspection - this would correspond to an expected 12500 true lenses (i.e. excluding contaminants) in Euclid DR1.

title: Two-dimensional galaxy cluster shapes using lensing data: a simulated analysis
comment: submitted to A&A, 16 pages, 9 figures; comments are welcome
summary: Context. Cluster morphology reflects assembly history and dynamical state. High-resolution weak lensing can reveal departures from spherical symmetry, but its ability to recover two-dimensional shapes remains less explored. Aims. We assess how reliably weak lensing recovers projected cluster morphology and its dependence on orientation and dynamical state. We also compare large-scale weak-lensing morphology with that traced by strong lensing near the cluster centre. Methods. We study three clusters at $z=0.22$ from The Three Hundred Project, representing relaxed, mildly disturbed and unrelaxed systems. For each, we consider three random projections and three along the principal axes of the mass tensor. For each projection, we generate 128 weak-lensing catalogues with a source density of 30 arcmin$^{-2}$ and intrinsic ellipticity dispersion $σ_ε=0.3$. We constrain mass and concentration from one-dimensional NFW and BMO fits, then recover ellipticity, position angle and centre using a two-dimensional elliptical NFW model. We also measure morphology from true convergence maps, Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions and strong-lensing tangential critical lines. Results. Recovered parameters depend on orientation and dynamical state. The relaxed cluster has similar inner and large-scale shapes, whereas disturbed systems appear more elliptical centrally. Two-dimensional weak-lensing modelling recovers the projected mass orientation despite source sampling and shape noise. Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions recover the position angle well but favour rounder mass distributions. Centroid offsets are larger in unrelaxed systems. Conclusions. Combining weak- and strong-lensing morphology probes cluster structure across physical scales and offers a promising way to investigate morphology and dynamical state.

title: Constraining the Inner Dark Matter Profiles of Strong-Lensing Galaxy Clusters
summary: We present mass modeling of three strong lensing galaxy clusters found in the Dark Energy Survey utilizing Hubble Space Telescope imaging for lens modeling, and complementary constraints from Chandra X-ray observations. All three clusters are relaxed and have giant arc or ring lens structures ideal for constraints on the dark matter distribution. The strong lens modeling and X-ray temperatures yield consistent total cluster mass estimates. We find these clusters have best-fit X-ray temperatures of $2.7 - 6.2$ keV and total masses of M$_{200} = (1-6) \times 10^{14} M_{\odot}$. Our lens models parameterize dark matter distribution with a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White (GNFW) density profile. While the GNFW profile allows the inner dark matter slope to vary, we find in all cases that the inner slopes are consistent with the standard NFW density profile $γ^{DM} = 1$. The X-ray surface brightness distributions for all three clusters are generally symmetric with no significant substructure, supporting the conclusion that these are relaxed clusters. In addition, we find generally low values of the external shear magnitude with median values ranging $|γ^{ext}| = 0.04-0.09$ and consistent with zero for two of the clusters.

title: SN Ares: A Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at $\mathbf{z=1.276}$ with a Predicted 70-Year Time Delay
comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the discovery of supernova (SN) Ares, a strongly lensed supernova at $z_{\rm spec}=1.276\pm0.002$ in a massive, triply imaged host galaxy behind the MACS J0308.9+2645 galaxy cluster. JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy spanning the rest-frame optical to NIR of Ares reveals helium features at $5876\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, $7065\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, and $10830\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, as well as H$α$ and Pa$β$. A comparison to local core-collapse SN spectra and light curves leads to a classification of SN Ares as a Type IIb supernova, the highest-redshift member of its class spectroscopically identified. A comparison to local SN IIb light curves provides a phase estimate for the spectrum of $34_{-9}^{+10}$ rest-frame days post-radioactive peak, providing a unique view into a high-redshift stripped-envelope supernova in its late-photospheric evolution. A lens model of the cluster constructed using recent JWST data indicates that SN Ares is the first image to arrive and will reappear in two future images near the center of the cluster plane in $\gtrsim 70$ years, with predicted magnifications of $\sim5\times$ and $\sim1.5\times$. Planned JWST/NIRSpec Multi-Object Spectroscopy of the cluster will allow for more detailed modeling of the lensed system for tighter constraints on the time delay and magnifications, as well as a template spectrum at the location of SN Ares.

title: Semi-Analytic Predictions for Strong-Lensing Perturbers in Cold and Self-Interacting Dark Matter
summary: Strong gravitational lensing is sensitive to the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos, providing a probe of gravothermal evolution in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM). We combine semi-analytic cold dark matter (CDM) subhalo histories with a model for gravothermal evolution in SIDM to generate CDM and SIDM subhalo populations across SIDM parameter space. We predict their projected enclosed masses and deflection-based projected density slopes and compare them with three perturbers inferred through gravitational imaging in PJ011646, SDSS J0946+1006, and JVAS B1938+666. For SIDM model parameters $σ_0/m_χ=147.1$ cm$^2$/g and $w=120$ km/s, SIDM subhalos reproduce all three perturbers more often than CDM subhalos. For PJ011646, we find ~0.6 cored SIDM subhalos per host matching the perturber, compared with ~0.002 in CDM, while core-collapsed subhalos are too steep. For SDSS J0946+1006, we find ~3 core-collapsed and ~0.004 cored SIDM subhalos per host, compared with none in 900 CDM realizations, although baryons, neglected here, may matter for such massive subhalos. For "detection V" in JVAS B1938+666, we find ~220 core-collapsed and ~20 cored SIDM subhalos per host within the $2σ$ posterior region, compared with ~0.2 in CDM; the CDM candidates require exceptionally early accretion, at median redshift $z\sim13$. Simultaneously reproducing all three perturbers requires $w\gtrsim10^2$ km/s, so that the massive (~$5.6\times10^{10}M_\odot$) progenitors of SDSS J0946+1006 candidates can collapse, and is achieved for $σ_0/m_χ\gtrsim10^2$ cm$^2$/g in the parameter sets studied. Our results show how semi-analytic models can quantify how often subhalos reproduce individual perturbers in different dark matter models, and our modular framework can be readily updated as models of tidal stripping and late-stage gravothermal evolution in SIDM improve. title: Gamma-ray Bursts as Cosmological Probes Calibrated with Strongly Lensed Quasars and Neural Networks
summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend distance measurements to redshifts beyond those routinely probed by Type Ia supernovae, but their use in cosmology is limited by calibration circularity and possible redshift-dependent effects. We investigate strongly lensed quasars as external calibrators of the Amati and Combo GRB relations. We reconstruct the luminosity-distance relation using an artificial neural network trained on TDCOSMO strong-lensing distances, with the absolute scale inherited from the lensing-only calibration. To avoid extrapolation, only GRBs within the lens-supported redshift interval are used for calibration. We then infer cosmological parameters through a hierarchical Bayesian analysis of flat $Λ$CDM, with $w_0w_a$CDM examined as a consistency test. For flat $Λ$CDM, Amati yields $H_0=78.26^{+17.87}_{-16.30}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $Ω_m=0.670^{+0.223}_{-0.276}$, while Combo yields $H_0=78.71^{+13.83}_{-11.29}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $Ω_m=0.635^{+0.235}_{-0.242}$. Amati is relatively insensitive to the phenomenological redshift term, whereas Combo shows a stronger dependence. Injection--recovery tests indicate that an unmodelled positive Combo trend can bias $H_0$ and $Ω_m$ upward. Strong-lens calibration therefore offers a route to extending the GRB Hubble diagram, but the inferred $H_0$ is not an independent GRB measurement: it retains the TDCOSMO distance scale. The precision is limited by GRB scatter, redshift-dependent systematics, and lens-modelling uncertainties.

title: Late-time distance consistency and model-independent curvature inference with strong lensing, quasars, and galaxy clusters
comment: 18 pages, 6 figures, Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA)
summary: We revisit a late-time, model-independent distance-consistency framework that combines strong gravitational lensing systems (SGLS), ultraviolet/X-ray quasars (QSOs), and 38 Sunyaev--Zel'dovich/X-ray galaxy-cluster angular-diameter distances. The analysis focuses on systematics rather than on presenting a competitive curvature measurement. Starting from the 158-system SGLS catalog, we exclude 30 systems that violate the lensing-geometric requirement $D_{A,ls}/D_{A,s}<1$ in the isothermal reference case $γ_{\rm lens}=2$, leaving a fixed 128-system SGLS parent sample for cross-matching with 1598 QSOs. A deterministic maximum-cardinality, minimum-mismatch one-to-one assignment yields 100 SGLS--QSO pairs at the nominal $Δd/d=5\%$ threshold. We propagate the measured X-ray flux uncertainties and the intrinsic QSO scatter, and, crucially, we include the full $38\times38$ covariance induced by using the same QSO distances in the kernel-smoothed cluster predictions. With $Ω_K\sim\mathcal{U}[-10,10]$, the joint posterior is $Ω_K=2.085^{+1.634}_{-1.103}$ (68\%; central 95\% interval $[0.269,6.028]$). We do not interpret the positive shift as evidence for an open Universe. \added{This positive posterior offset is driven by cross-probe calibration tensions, sample-assignment effects, and the cluster anchor; it cannot be attributed to the intrinsic spatial geometry of the Universe.} The SGLS+QSO data alone leave curvature essentially prior dominated, $Ω_K=0.70^{+6.33}_{-7.12}$, whereas removing only the off-diagonal cluster covariance moves the posterior to $Ω_K=5.21^{+2.46}_{-2.07}$. Thus the cluster anchor supplies most of the curvature constraining power and its covariance materially changes the posterior location.

title: Statistical Strong Lensing V. Inference with Microlensed Quasars
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Microlensing of strongly lensed quasars provides direct information on the stellar component of lens galaxies, and can help break the degeneracy between the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and the dark matter. However, a statistical framework to forward model microlensing data while accounting for strong lensing selection effects is still missing. We incorporated microlensing effects into the hierarchical model of Paper III, and investigated to what extent flux measurements of strongly lensed quasars can break the degeneracy between the stellar IMF and the dark matter distribution. We tested the method on a mock sample of 219 doubly imaged quasars, lensed by circularly symmetric lenses. When microlensing effects are modelled, the inference using image fluxes recovers the input foreground population parameters and provides tighter constraints than the inference without flux constraints. The improvement is clearest in the $μ_α-μ_5$ plane, where $μ_α$ describes the mean stellar population synthesis mismatch parameter $\logα_{\rm SPS}$ and $μ_5$ describes the mean projected dark matter mass within $5\,{\rm kpc}$. The 68% credible interval on $μ_α$ shrinks from 0.16 dex to 0.09 dex, with the degeneracy between $μ_α$ and $μ_5$ significantly reduced. By contrast, fitting the image fluxes without accounting for microlensing leads to large biases on the inferred parameters. This work is a first step towards an accurate modelling of microlensing data. Application to real lens samples will require dropping the circular symmetry assumption and adopting more realistic models for the microlensing magnification.

title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Space-borne Detectors
comment: 20 pages, 13 figures, 11 tables, to appear in ApJS
summary: Future space-borne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of space-borne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as \textbf{GW-LMC-Space}. Our results show that, for a four-year LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from $0$ to $131$, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to $\sim 0.3\%$. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a one-year observation is expected to lie in the range of $0$--$44$, with a lensing probability of $\sim 0.15\%$ for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). We further show that the overlap of lensed signals is a common feature in space-borne detectors, which can significantly affect both the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimation and event identification. These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future space-borne GW observations.

title: Tracing small-scale structure formation through cosmic time with strong gravitational lensing: A case for a next-generation sub-millimetre/millimetre interferometer
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series
summary: The nature of dark matter and the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in modern astrophysics. Both leave a key signature in an overlapping, largely unexplored mass range: $<10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ dark haloes and wandering black holes. These may be undetectable directly, but detectable through gravitational perturbation of strongly lensed images, and partly or entirely distinguishable from one another through lensing data alone. We demonstrate through realistic simulations that a 255-element sub-mm/mm interferometer could probe this critical mass regime, detecting gravitational perturbations in strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) from objects down to at least $10^5$ M$_{\odot}$. Combined with lens-galaxy characterisation from the European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which strengthens the physical interpretation of detected perturbers, and the unprecedented lens samples expected from Euclid and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), this facility could deliver a census of low-mass dark matter haloes and wandering massive black holes across cosmic time.

title: Strong gravitational lensing with Euclid
comment: Contribution to the Focus Point ''Surprises from major new telescopes''
summary: Euclid data is going to lead to the discovery of approximately 10^5 new strong gravitational lenses, thereby increasing the number of known lenses by a factor of 30. Such an impressive jump has the potential to revolutionise the field of strong lensing, by covering an ever-increasing range in the parameter space occupied by the lenses and lensed sources, and by uncovering rare and precious strong lens systems. The first quick data release of Euclid has already revealed hundreds of lenses, giving us a taste of what the final Euclid strong lens sample might look like. These lenses include a variety of objects acting as deflectors, from isolated galaxies to clusters, from early-type galaxies to edge-on disks. As many as four double-source plane lenses, in which one foreground object lenses two galaxies at two different redshifts, have already been discovered. As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

title: Microcaustics: Fast GPU-Accelerated Dynamical Microlensing of Time-Dependent Extended Sources
comment: 26 pages, 11 figures. Code available at https://github.com/JFagin/microcaustics
summary: Gravitational microlensing probes unresolved quasar accretion disc structure and compact objects in lens galaxies and is an important systematic in strong-lens time-delay cosmography. Most analyses use static microlensing map simulations because evolving individual microlenses and caustics is computationally prohibitive. We present Microcaustics, a GPU-accelerated Python package built on PyTorch for dynamical microlensing of time-dependent extended sources in strong gravitational lenses. It combines a local-exact/far-field deflection solver, source-directed lens-plane scouting with temporal reuse, and biquadratic inverse polygon mapping (IPM). GPU batching and fused Triton rasterization accelerate the calculation, while binary caustic labels track source-centred crossings. Across three simulated quadruply lensed quasar systems, our package generates a 10-year, 147-frame multiband light curve in an amortized median of 0.68 s (0.88 s with labels) on a consumer GPU with a median light-curve RMSE of 0.35 mmag, while recovering every reference source-centred caustic crossing. At comparable map accuracy, the batched throughput is 780 times higher than that of a recent CUDA IPM implementation and extrapolates to a speedup of millions relative to classic GPU-D. We demonstrate that our IPM converges as $N_{\rm ray}^{-0.84}$, approaching the idealized $N_{\rm ray}^{-1}$ convergence rate of piecewise-affine IPM and improving upon the $N_{\rm ray}^{-1/2}$ inverse ray-shooting rate. We also introduce a GPU-resident general relativistic and reverberating quasar source model and demonstrate our method with an evolving supernova source. These advances make fully dynamical stellar fields practical for Bayesian and simulation-based inference.

AI.tldr: Microcaustics：一个基于 PyTorch 的 GPU 加速 Python 软件包，实现强引力透镜中时变延展源的动态微透镜模拟，可在消费级 GPU 上高效生成含微焦散交叉的多波段光变曲线。

AI.method: 提出 Microcaustics 软件包，基于 PyTorch 与 GPU 加速。方法整合了局部精确/远场偏转求解器、带时间复用的源导向透镜平面探测，以及双二次反多边形映射（IPM）；利用 GPU 批处理与融合 Triton 光栅化加速计算，并用二元焦散标签追踪以源为中心的交叉，同时引入 GPU 常驻的广义相对论与混响类星体源模型。
AI.result: 在三个模拟的四重透镜类星体系统上，软件包生成 10 年、147 帧多波段光变曲线，消费级 GPU 上摊销中位耗时 0.68 s（含标签 0.88 s），光变曲线 RMSE 中位为 0.35 mmag，并能恢复全部参考源中心焦散交叉。相同图精度下，批处理吞吐量比近期 CUDA IPM 实现高 780 倍，相对经典 GPU-D 外推可达百万倍加速。IPM 收敛率为 N_ray^-0.84，接近分段仿射 IPM 的理想 N_ray^-1，优于逆向光线射击的 N_ray^-1/2。

title: Cosmology with strong gravitational lenses
comment: Reviews of Modern Physics, invited article; 59 pages, 32 figures
summary: Three of the most pressing open questions in cosmology -- the nature of dark energy and dark matter, and the growing tension in the value of the Hubble constant H$_0$ -- call for cosmological probes that are independent of, and complementary to, traditional methods. Strong gravitational lensing offers exactly that: a purely gravitational probe of the universe's expansion history and matter distribution, sensitive to dark matter's presence regardless of whether it interacts with light. Time-delay lenses and multiplane lenses can measure H$_0$ and the dark energy equation of state directly, while the distortion of lensed images can reveal the abundance and internal structure of dark matter subhalos. After a brief theoretical and historical introduction, I review recent breakthroughs enabled by JWST and by advances in lens modeling and stellar dynamics. Examples include the recent measurement of H$_0$ with 3\% precision in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology, and a tentative detection of dark matter self-interaction. Strong lensing is entering a pivotal era: wide-field surveys with Euclid, Rubin, and Roman, and radio surveys with the Square Kilometer Array, are poised to increase the number of known strong lenses by orders of magnitude, positioning strong lensing to play a central role in answering these open questions in the decade ahead.

title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
comment: 8 pages, 4 figues, 1 table; submitted to A&A
summary: We present the first inference of the Hubble constant and matter density parameter from a strongly lensed supernova (SN) by exploiting the mass model of a galaxy cluster enhanced by an extended surface brightness reconstruction. This has resulted in the most precise H0 measurement from a single strong lens so far, outperforming the 3.9% result from the lensed quasar DES J048-5354. Building upon the mass model of MACS J1149.5+2223 relying on image positions only, we incorporate the surface brightness distribution of the SN Refsdal host, to infer some cosmological parameter values within a flat LCDM framework. We consider two cosmological parameterizations, with either H0 and $Ω_m$ or H0 alone treated as free parameters. We explore four different mass-model realizations to assess some of the systematic uncertainties associated with the constraint weighting and source reconstruction. Although known as one of the main systematic effects, we deliberately keep the cluster total mass parametrization fixed to that of the previously published point-like mass model to enable a fair comparison. This reveals that incorporating 77,000 HST pixels reduces the uncertainty on the inferred value of H0 by a factor of 2.0. Our final measurements are $H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc and $Ω_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, in agreement with previous results from lensed SNe. This corresponds to a substantially improved precision, reaching a remarkable 3.0% uncertainty on the value of H0. The contributions of the uncertainties on the lens total mass and on the measured time delays to the final H0 error are now comparable, indicating that future improvements will depend on more precise time-delay measurements and continued control of systematic effects. With sub-percent time-delay values reachable at cluster-scale, this mass model approach has the power to lead to unprecedentedly precise H0 measurements.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们首次通过利用扩展表面亮度重建增强的星系团质量模型，从强透镜超新星（SN）推断哈勃常数和物质密度参数。这产生了迄今为止从单一强透镜获得的最精确的H0测量，优于透镜类星体DES J048-5354的3.9%结果。基于仅依赖图像位置的MACS J1149.5+2223质量模型，我们纳入SN Refsdal宿主的表面亮度分布，在平坦LCDM框架内推断一些宇宙学参数值。我们考虑两种宇宙学参数化，其中H0和$Ω_m$或仅H0被视为自由参数。我们探索四种不同的质量模型实现，以评估与约束加权和源重建相关的一些系统不确定性。尽管已知是主要系统效应之一，我们故意将星系团总质量参数化固定为先前发表的类点质量模型，以便进行公平比较。这表明纳入77,000个HST像素将推断的H0值的不确定性降低了2.0倍。我们的最终测量结果为$H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc和$Ω_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$，与先前透镜超新星的结果一致。这对应于显著提高的精度，达到H0值3.0%的不确定性。透镜总质量和测量时间延迟的不确定性对最终H0误差的贡献现在相当，表明未来的改进将取决于更精确的时间延迟测量和持续控制系统效应。在星系团尺度上可实现亚百分比时间延迟值的情况下，这种质量模型方法有能力导致前所未有的精确H0测量。

title: What fuels the growth of stars and black holes in galaxies through cosmic time? The physics and chemistry of the interstellar medium in distant galaxies
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series. 9 pages 3 figures
summary: The interplay between the baryonic matter in galaxies (gas, dust, stars) has a fundamental role in our understanding of galaxy formation and evolution through cosmic time. The (sub)mm regime provides a unique window to measure the physical conditions and chemistry in the cold and dusty gas reservoirs that fuel the formation of new stars and the growth of massive black holes in distant galaxies. Large sub(mm) interferometers have made a revolutionary impact mapping the cold gas and dust in galaxies beyond the local universe. However, significant progress is hampered by limited spectral-line sensitivity. After more than a decade of surveys, molecular gas (traced by 12CO) has been measured only in a few tens of typical, massive main-sequence star-forming galaxies at z>1, while access to fainter gas-tracing species has been limited to only the very brightest galaxies. Thereby it restricts access to the detailed conditions in the cold gas clouds in typical galaxies in the distant universe. A revolutionary, flagship sub-mm interferometer with a massive increase in instantaneous spectral line sensitivity and broad spectral grasp (ALMA2040) fills this gap by enabling rich, multi-transition, multi-species and multi-isotopologue studies of the atomic and molecular interstellar medium for thousands of typical galaxies across galaxy populations and redshift. This will unveil how the ISM evolves across the galaxy population for statistical samples in different redshift bins, detailed studies of the physical conditions and chemistry in the multi-phase interstellar medium of typical galaxies, and how the cold ISM regulates and responds to star- and black-hole formation, providing a tremendous leap forward in the study of galaxy assembly over cosmic time.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 星系中重子物质（气体、尘埃、恒星）之间的相互作用对于我们理解宇宙时间尺度上星系的形成与演化具有根本性的作用。（亚）毫米波段为测量冷而多尘的气体储库中的物理条件和化学性质提供了独特的窗口，这些气体储库为遥远星系中新恒星的形成和巨大黑洞的增长提供了燃料。大型亚毫米波干涉仪已经对本地宇宙之外星系中的冷气体和尘埃的测绘产生了革命性的影响。然而，显著的进展受到有限谱线灵敏度的阻碍。经过十多年的巡天，分子气体（由12CO示踪）仅在z>1的几十个典型的、大质量的主序恒星形成星系中被测量到，而获取更暗弱的示踪气体的种类仅限于最明亮的星系。因此，这限制了对遥远宇宙中典型星系冷气体云详细条件的获取。一个革命性的、旗舰级的亚毫米波干涉仪，具有瞬时谱线灵敏度的大幅提升和宽光谱覆盖（ALMA2040），通过使对数千个典型星系（涵盖不同星系族群和红移）的原子和分子星际介质进行丰富的、多跃迁、多物种和多同位素体研究成为可能，填补了这一空白。这将揭示星际介质如何在不同的红移区间内对统计样本的星系族群中演化，对典型星系多相星际介质的物理条件和化学性质的详细研究，以及冷星际介质如何调节和响应恒星和黑洞的形成，从而在宇宙时间尺度上星系组装的研究中实现巨大的飞跃。

title: Probing ordered magnetic fields in galaxies across cosmic time
comment: Part of the ALMA2040 White Paper Series, 10 pages, 3 figures, additional comments are welcome
summary: Magnetic fields are dynamically important across many astronomical environments, yet their origin, strength, and evolution over cosmic time remain poorly understood. Ordered magnetic fields are ubiquitous in the nearby Universe, as revealed by a range of observational techniques, but evidence for their existence at cosmological distances is scarce. Recent ALMA detections of polarised dust emission indicate that galactic-scale ordered magnetic fields, spanning up to kiloparsec scales, were already present in massive star-forming galaxies at redshifts up to $z\sim5.6$. This white paper argues that the ALMA2040 concept -- with its nearly tenfold improvement in sensitivity and angular resolution, and full-polarisation capability extended to higher-frequency bands -- will open up the study of cosmic magnetism in the early Universe. We identify four science drivers: constraining the dynamos that generate galactic-scale ordered fields, measuring the strength of early magnetic fields, connecting magnetic fields to galaxy evolution across cosmic time, and constraining dust grain properties through the polarised spectral energy distribution. We summarise the corresponding requirements in angular resolution, spectral coverage, and sensitivity, and discuss synergies with next-generation telescopes.

title: Resolved SED modelling with JWST and ALMA: the role of stellar mass surface density in regulating star formation in cosmic noon galaxies
comment: 26 pages, 15 figures, 5 tables. Published in MNRAS
summary: We present kpc-scale ($0.2''-0.5''$) physical property maps of 35 main-sequence galaxies at $z \approx 0.5-3.7$, with stellar masses of $\log(M_*/M_\odot) \sim 9.7-11.7$ and star formation rates of $\mathrm{SFR} \sim 1.4-280\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$, selected from the ALMA Spectroscopic Survey (ASPECS) in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. Leveraging the unique HST, JWST (NIRCam and MIRI), and ALMA observations, we perform spatially resolved spectral energy distribution (SED) modeling across the UV-to-FIR regime. We find that incorporating MIRI and/or ALMA data reduces the overestimation of dust luminosity (by up to $\sim0.8$ dex), while ALMA observations further mitigate the age-dust degeneracy. In the absence of such data, restricting the SED model library based on the observed unresolved colors can partially mitigate these biases. The stellar masses ($M_{*}$) derived from resolved and unresolved modeling are consistent within $\sim0.05$ dex, suggesting that mass discrepancies (attributed to outshining) are less significant for cosmic noon main-sequence galaxies when rest-frame near-infrared (NIR; e.g., $\sim1-3\,μ\mathrm{m}$) data are included. After normalization to the same reference, the composite SED of our sample closely resembles that of local starburst galaxies such as M82, suggesting similar dust attenuation and re-emission properties. Finally, we find that the molecular gas fraction and depletion time correlate with the effective stellar mass surface density ($Σ_{\rm eff,*} = M_{*}/2πR_{\rm eff,M_*}^2$) similarly to that observed in local galaxies. These results provide a first qualitative view of how the stellar gravitational potential influences gas regulation and star formation in galaxies beyond the local Universe.

artifacts.abstract_zh: 我们展示了35个位于$z \approx 0.5-3.7$的主序星系的kpc尺度（$0.2''-0.5''$）物理性质图，这些星系选自哈勃超深场中的ALMA光谱巡天（ASPECS），其恒星质量范围为$\log(M_*/M_\odot) \sim 9.7-11.7$，恒星形成率为$\mathrm{SFR} \sim 1.4-280\,\mathrm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$。利用独特的HST、JWST（NIRCam和MIRI）以及ALMA观测数据，我们在紫外到远红外波段进行了空间分辨的光谱能量分布（SED）建模。我们发现，纳入MIRI和/或ALMA数据可将尘埃光度的过高估计降低（最多约$\sim0.8$ dex），而ALMA观测进一步缓解了年龄-尘埃简并。在缺乏此类数据的情况下，基于观测到的未分辨颜色限制SED模型库可以部分缓解这些偏差。从分辨和未分辨建模得到的恒星质量（$M_{*}$）在$\sim0.05$ dex内一致，表明当包含静止系近红外（NIR；例如$\sim1-3\,μ\mathrm{m}$）数据时，对于宇宙正午的主序星系，质量差异（归因于outshining）并不显著。归一化到相同参考后，我们样本的复合SED与本地星暴星系（如M82）的SED非常相似，表明相似的尘埃衰减和再辐射性质。最后，我们发现分子气体分数和耗尽时间与有效恒星质量表面密度（$Σ_{\rm eff,*} = M_{*}/2πR_{\rm eff,M_*}^2$）的相关性与在本地星系中观测到的类似。这些结果首次定性地展示了恒星引力势如何影响本地宇宙之外星系中的气体调节和恒星形成。
